name: Oregon

events.title: Statehood
events.text: Oregon became the 33rd state on February 14, 1859. Congress gave it 1 seat in the House until the next apportionment.

events.title: 1860 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1860 census, Oregon kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1870 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1870 census, Oregon kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1880 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1880 census, Oregon kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1890 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1890 census, Oregon's House delegation grew from 1 to 2 seats.

events.title: 1900 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1900 census, Oregon kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1910 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1910 census, Oregon's House delegation grew from 2 to 3 seats.

events.title: 1930 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1930 census, Oregon kept 3 seats in the House.

events.title: 1940 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1940 census, Oregon's House delegation grew from 3 to 4 seats.

events.title: 1950 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1950 census, Oregon kept 4 seats in the House.

events.title: 1960 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1960 census, Oregon kept 4 seats in the House.

events.title: 1970 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1970 census, Oregon kept 4 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1980 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1980 census, Oregon's House delegation grew from 4 to 5 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1990 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1990 census, Oregon kept 5 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Court draws map after veto
events.text: The governor vetoed the legislature's plan in June 2001. A state circuit court then drew the congressional districts on October 19, 2001, in Perrin v. Kitzhaber.

events.title: 2000 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2000 census, Oregon kept 5 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 2010 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2010 census, Oregon kept 5 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Six-district map upheld by judicial panel
events.text: The legislature passed a map adding a sixth district in September 2021. A five-judge state court panel unanimously dismissed a challenge on November 24, 2021, finding the challengers had not proven an unlawful partisan gerrymander.

events.title: 2020 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2020 census, Oregon's House delegation grew from 5 to 6 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.

c053.text: New map drawn after the 1890 census, which raised Oregon's seats from 1 to 2. It was first used in the 1892 election.

c063.text: New map drawn after the 1910 census, which raised Oregon's seats from 2 to 3. It was first used in the 1912 election.

c078.text: New map drawn after the 1940 census, which raised Oregon's seats from 3 to 4. It was first used in the 1942 election.

c090.text: Oregon's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1966 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c093.text: New map drawn after the 1970 census, which left Oregon with 4 seats. It was first used in the 1972 election.

c098.text: New map drawn after the 1980 census, which raised Oregon's seats from 4 to 5. It was first used in the 1982 election.

c103.text: New map drawn after the 1990 census, which left Oregon with 5 seats. It was first used in the 1992 election.

c108.text: New map following: Court draws map after veto. The governor vetoed the legislature's plan in June 2001. A state circuit court then drew the congressional districts on October 19, 2001, in Perrin v. Kitzhaber.

c113.text: New map drawn after the 2010 census, which left Oregon with 5 seats. It was first used in the 2012 election.

c115.text: Not a new map: the historical boundary records show only slight differences in 2 districts from the previous Congress, and no statewide redistricting is recorded for this election.

c118.text: New map following: Six-district map upheld by judicial panel. The legislature passed a map adding a sixth district in September 2021. A five-judge state court panel unanimously dismissed a challenge on November 24, 2021, finding the challengers had not proven an unlawful partisan gerrymander.
